title: UP BOARD CLASS 8 — Physics | Fluid Pressure Atmospheric
description: Subject-wise test on Fluid Pressure Atmospheric (Physics) for UP BOARD CLASS 8. 25Q.
subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: The force acting perpendicularly on a unit area of a surface is called:

options.text: Thrust
options.explanation: Thrust is the total force acting perpendicular to a surface, not per unit area.

options.text: Friction
options.explanation: Friction is a force that opposes motion between two surfaces in contact.

options.text: Pressure
options.explanation: Correct. Pressure is force per unit area.

options.text: Gravity
options.explanation: Gravity is the force of attraction between two masses.

questions.explanation: Pressure is defined as the force (specifically, thrust) acting per unit area of a surface.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: Which of the following is the SI unit of pressure?

options.text: Newton (N)
options.explanation: Newton is the SI unit of force, not pressure.

options.text: Joule (J)
options.explanation: Joule is the SI unit of energy or work.

options.text: Pascal (Pa)
options.explanation: Correct. Pascal is the SI unit of pressure.

options.text: Watt (W)
options.explanation: Watt is the SI unit of power.

questions.explanation: The SI unit of pressure is Pascal (Pa), which is equivalent to one Newton per square meter (N/m²).
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a non-contact force?

options.text: Frictional force
options.explanation: Frictional force requires contact between surfaces.

options.text: Muscular force
options.explanation: Muscular force is applied through physical contact.

options.text: Electrostatic force
options.explanation: Correct. Electrostatic force acts at a distance without contact.

options.text: Normal force
options.explanation: Normal force is exerted when two objects are in contact.

questions.explanation: Electrostatic force acts between charged objects even when they are not in physical contact. Frictional, muscular, and normal forces require direct contact between objects.
questions.hint: Non-contact forces do not require physical interaction between objects.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: When we apply force to an object, it can change its: I. Speed II. Direction of motion III. Shape IV. Mass

options.text: I and II only
options.explanation: Force can also change the shape of an object.

options.text: I, II and IV only
options.explanation: Force does not change the mass of an object.

options.text: I, II and III only
options.explanation: Correct. Force can change speed, direction, and shape.

options.text: All of the above
options.explanation: Force does not change the mass of an object.

questions.explanation: Force can change an object's speed, direction of motion, or shape. However, force does not change the mass of an object.
questions.hint: Force affects motion and structure but not the fundamental property of mass.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: It is easier to cut vegetables with a sharp knife than with a blunt knife because:

options.text: A sharp knife is usually heavier.
options.explanation: Weight does not directly affect cutting ease.

options.text: A sharp knife has a larger surface area to apply force.
options.explanation: A sharp knife has a smaller surface area.

options.text: A sharp knife has a smaller contact area, thus exerting more pressure for the same force.
options.explanation: Correct. Smaller area increases pressure.

options.text: A sharp knife requires less muscular force.
options.explanation: Muscular force may be similar, but pressure is the key factor.

questions.explanation: Pressure is inversely proportional to the area of contact (P = F/A). A sharp knife has a very small cutting edge (area), so for the same applied force, it exerts much greater pressure, making it easier to cut.
questions.hint: Consider how the area of contact affects pressure for the same applied force.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: The pressure exerted by a liquid at a certain depth:

options.text: Decreases with increasing depth.
options.explanation: Pressure increases with depth.

options.text: Is the same at all points within the liquid.
options.explanation: Pressure varies with depth.

options.text: Increases with increasing depth.
options.explanation: Correct. Pressure increases with depth.

options.text: Depends only on the surface area of the liquid.
options.explanation: Pressure depends on depth and density, not surface area.

questions.explanation: Liquid pressure increases with depth because the column of liquid above that point becomes taller, meaning there is more weight (force) per unit area pressing down.
questions.hint: Think about the weight of the liquid column above a point.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: A force of 200 N is applied uniformly on a surface of area 4 m². What is the pressure exerted on the surface?

options.text: 20 Pa
options.explanation: Incorrect calculation.

options.text: 40 Pa
options.explanation: Incorrect calculation.

options.text: 50 Pa
options.explanation: Correct. P = 200 N / 4 m² = 50 Pa.

options.text: 800 Pa
options.explanation: Incorrect calculation.

questions.explanation: Pressure (P) = Force (F) / Area (A) = 200 N / 4 m² = 50 N/m² = 50 Pa.
questions.hint: Use the formula P = F/A.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: A suction cup sticks to a smooth, non-porous surface primarily due to:

options.text: Adhesive properties of the rubber.
options.explanation: Adhesion may help, but the primary reason is pressure difference.

options.text: The vacuum created inside the cup pulling it.
options.explanation: A vacuum does not 'pull'; it is the external pressure that pushes.

options.text: The greater atmospheric pressure acting on the outside of the cup compared to the pressure inside.
options.explanation: Correct. Atmospheric pressure pushes the cup against the surface.

options.text: Magnetic forces between the cup and the surface.
options.explanation: Suction cups do not rely on magnetic forces.

questions.explanation: When a suction cup is pressed, air is expelled, creating a region of lower pressure inside. The higher atmospheric pressure acting on the outside of the cup then pushes it firmly against the surface.
questions.hint: Consider the role of atmospheric pressure in suction cups.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: Assertion (A): Wide shoulder straps on school bags are more comfortable than thin straps. Reason (R): Wide straps distribute the weight over a larger area, reducing the pressure on the shoulders.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Correct. Both statements are true, and R explains A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R correctly explains A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true; wide straps are more comfortable. The reason is also true and correctly explains the assertion: by increasing the contact area, the pressure (Force/Area) exerted by the bag's weight on the shoulders is reduced, making it less painful.
questions.hint: Consider how pressure is related to area and comfort.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: Two containers, P and Q, are filled with different liquids. Container P has water (density = 1000 kg/m³) filled to a height of 0.5 m. Container Q has oil (density = 800 kg/m³) filled to a height of 0.7 m. Assuming g = 10 m/s², which container experiences greater pressure at its bottom?

options.text: Container P
options.explanation: Container P has lower pressure (5000 Pa).

options.text: Container Q
options.explanation: Container Q has higher pressure (5600 Pa).

options.text: Both experience the same pressure
options.explanation: Pressures are different.

options.text: Cannot be determined without knowing the base area.
options.explanation: Pressure at the bottom depends only on height, density, and gravity.

questions.explanation: Pressure exerted by a liquid (P) = h × ρ × g. For Container P: P_P = 0.5 × 1000 × 10 = 5000 Pa. For Container Q: P_Q = 0.7 × 800 × 10 = 5600 Pa. Since P_Q > P_P, Container Q experiences greater pressure.
questions.hint: Use the formula P = h × ρ × g to calculate pressure for both containers.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: Which of the following describes the push or pull on an object?

options.text: Pressure
options.explanation: Pressure is force per unit area, not the push or pull itself.

options.text: Thrust
options.explanation: Thrust is a specific type of force, usually associated with propulsion.

options.text: Force
options.explanation: Force is the correct term for a push or pull on an object.

options.text: Area
options.explanation: Area is a measure of surface, not a push or pull.

questions.explanation: A force is defined as a push or a pull acting on an object, which can change its state of motion or shape.
questions.hint: Think about the basic definition of force.

questions.question: The SI unit of pressure is:

options.text: Newton
options.explanation: Newton is the SI unit of force, not pressure.

options.text: Joule
options.explanation: Joule is the SI unit of energy or work, not pressure.

options.text: Pascal
options.explanation: Pascal (Pa) is the SI unit of pressure.

options.text: Watt
options.explanation: Watt is the SI unit of power, not pressure.

questions.explanation: Pressure is defined as force per unit area. The SI unit for force is Newton (N) and for area is square meter (m²). Therefore, the SI unit for pressure is N/m², which is also known as Pascal (Pa).
questions.hint: Recall the formula for pressure: Pressure = Force/Area.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a non-contact force?

options.text: Frictional force
options.explanation: Frictional force requires physical contact between surfaces.

options.text: Magnetic force
options.explanation: Magnetic force acts at a distance without physical contact.

options.text: Muscular force
options.explanation: Muscular force requires physical contact to exert force.

options.text: Force applied by stretching a spring
options.explanation: This is a contact force as it involves physical interaction with the spring.

questions.explanation: Non-contact forces are those that act on an object without physically touching it. Magnetic force, gravitational force, and electrostatic force are examples of non-contact forces. Frictional force, muscular force, and the force from a spring are contact forces.
questions.hint: Non-contact forces do not require physical interaction.

questions.question: A sharp knife cuts vegetables more easily than a blunt knife because:

options.text: It applies more force.
options.explanation: Both knives apply roughly the same force; the difference is in the area of contact.

options.text: It has a smaller area of contact, thus increasing pressure.
options.explanation: A smaller area increases pressure for the same force, making cutting easier.

options.text: It reduces the resistance of the vegetable.
options.explanation: The resistance of the vegetable is not directly related to the knife's sharpness in this context.

options.text: It has a larger area of contact, thus decreasing pressure.
options.explanation: A larger area would decrease pressure, making cutting harder.

questions.explanation: Pressure is inversely proportional to the area over which the force is applied (P = F/A). A sharp knife has a very small cutting edge (area), so for the same amount of force applied, it exerts a much greater pressure, making it easier to cut.
questions.hint: Consider the relationship between pressure, force, and area.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: Atmospheric pressure is the pressure exerted by:

options.text: The weight of water in the atmosphere.
options.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is due to air, not water.

options.text: The force of gravity on Earth.
options.explanation: Gravity is the force that causes the weight of the air column, but it is not the pressure itself.

options.text: The weight of the air column above us.
options.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column above us.

options.text: The gases within a sealed container.
options.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is not confined to sealed containers.

questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is caused by the weight of the enormous column of air extending from the Earth's surface to the top of the atmosphere. This weight exerts a pressure on everything beneath it.
questions.hint: Think about what makes up the atmosphere and how it exerts pressure.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: A force of 50 N is applied over an area of 0.5 m². Calculate the pressure exerted.

options.text: 25 Pa
options.explanation: 25 Pa is incorrect; the calculation yields 100 Pa.

options.text: 50 Pa
options.explanation: 50 Pa is incorrect; the calculation yields 100 Pa.

options.text: 75 Pa
options.explanation: 75 Pa is incorrect; the calculation yields 100 Pa.

options.text: 100 Pa
options.explanation: The correct pressure is 100 Pa.

questions.explanation: Given: Force (F) = 50 N, Area (A) = 0.5 m². Pressure (P) = Force (F) / Area (A) = 50 N / 0.5 m² = 100 N/m² = 100 Pa.
questions.hint: Use the formula Pressure = Force/Area.

questions.question: Why do wide straps make it easier to carry heavy bags?

options.text: They increase the total force exerted by the bag.
options.explanation: The total force (weight) remains the same; straps do not change the weight.

options.text: They decrease the weight of the bag.
options.explanation: Straps do not change the weight of the bag.

options.text: They increase the area of contact, thereby reducing the pressure on the shoulders.
options.explanation: Increasing the area reduces pressure, making it easier to carry.

options.text: They allow the bag to move more freely.
options.explanation: The movement of the bag is not the primary reason for comfort.

questions.explanation: Wide straps distribute the weight (force) of the bag over a larger area of the shoulder. Since Pressure = Force/Area, increasing the area of contact reduces the pressure on the shoulder, making it more comfortable to carry the bag.
questions.hint: Consider how pressure changes with area for the same force.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: Which of the following statements about fluid pressure is INCORRECT?

options.text: Pressure exerted by a fluid increases with depth.
options.explanation: This statement is correct; pressure increases with depth.

options.text: Pressure exerted by a fluid acts in all directions.
options.explanation: This statement is correct; fluid pressure acts equally in all directions.

options.text: Pressure exerted by a fluid depends on the density of the fluid.
options.explanation: This statement is correct; pressure depends on fluid density.

options.text: Pressure exerted by a fluid depends on the shape of the container.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect; pressure does not depend on the shape of the container.

questions.explanation: Fluid pressure at a certain depth depends on the depth, the density of the fluid, and acceleration due to gravity (P = hρg). It does not depend on the shape or cross-sectional area of the container, as long as the depth is the same.
questions.hint: Fluid pressure depends on depth, density, and gravity, not container shape.

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** It is difficult to suck cold drinks with a straw on the Moon. **Reason (R):** There is no atmosphere on the Moon.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both are true, but R is not the direct explanation for A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true, but R does not directly explain why sucking is difficult.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

questions.explanation: Assertion A is true: Sucking with a straw works by reducing the air pressure inside the straw. The higher atmospheric pressure outside then pushes the liquid up the straw. On the Moon, there is no atmosphere, so there's no external atmospheric pressure to push the liquid up, making it difficult to suck. Reason R is also true: The Moon indeed has no atmosphere. However, R is not the *direct* explanation for why it's difficult to suck *cold drinks*. The reason is the *absence of atmospheric pressure* to push the liquid, which is a consequence of having no atmosphere.
questions.hint: Consider how a straw works and the role of atmospheric pressure.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: A diver experiences greater pressure as she dives deeper into the ocean. This is primarily due to:

options.text: Increased density of water at greater depths.
options.explanation: While density can vary slightly, it is not the primary reason for increased pressure.

options.text: Stronger gravitational force at greater depths.
options.explanation: Gravity is essentially constant at these depths and does not significantly increase.

options.text: The weight of the additional column of water above her.
options.explanation: The increased column of water above increases the pressure due to its weight.

options.text: The presence of more dissolved salts in deeper water.
options.explanation: Dissolved salts do not significantly affect pressure in this context.

questions.explanation: As the diver goes deeper, the column of water above her increases. The weight of this additional column of water exerts a greater force over her body, leading to an increase in pressure. While water density can slightly vary and gravity is essentially constant at these depths, the primary factor for increased pressure is the height of the fluid column (P = hρg).
questions.hint: Consider how the weight of the water above affects pressure.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: What is the pressure exerted by the air around us called?

options.text: Fluid Pressure
options.explanation: Fluid pressure refers to the pressure exerted by any fluid, not specifically the air around us.

options.text: Gravitational Pressure
options.explanation: Gravitational pressure is not a standard term; pressure due to gravity is part of fluid pressure but not specific to air.

options.text: Atmospheric Pressure
options.explanation: Correct. Atmospheric pressure is the pressure exerted by the air around us.

options.text: Magnetic Pressure
options.explanation: Magnetic pressure refers to pressure exerted by magnetic fields, unrelated to air pressure.

questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is defined as the pressure exerted by the column of air present above us at any given point.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: Why are the shoulder straps of school bags made wide?

options.text: To make them look more attractive.
options.explanation: Aesthetics are not the primary reason for the design of shoulder straps.

options.text: To increase the force exerted by the bag on the shoulders.
options.explanation: Increasing force would increase pressure, which is undesirable.

options.text: To reduce the pressure on the shoulders.
options.explanation: Correct. Wider straps increase the area, reducing pressure for comfort.

options.text: To make them easier to grip.
options.explanation: Grip is not the primary concern for shoulder straps.

questions.explanation: Pressure is inversely proportional to the area over which a force acts (P = F/A). By making the shoulder straps wide, the area of contact with the shoulders increases. This distributes the weight (force) of the bag over a larger area, thereby reducing the pressure experienced by the shoulders, making it more comfortable to carry.
questions.hint: Consider the relationship between pressure, force, and area.

questions.question: A diver experiences significantly greater pressure as they go deeper into the ocean. This is primarily because:

options.text: The density of seawater decreases with depth.
options.explanation: Density changes minimally with depth and does not primarily cause the pressure increase.

options.text: The atmospheric pressure increases with depth.
options.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is negligible compared to water pressure at depth.

options.text: The height of the water column above the diver increases with depth.
options.explanation: Correct. The taller water column increases the pressure due to its weight.

options.text: The temperature of the water decreases with depth.
options.explanation: Temperature changes do not directly cause the increase in pressure.

questions.explanation: The pressure exerted by a fluid increases with depth because the weight of the fluid column above that point increases. As a diver goes deeper, the column of water above them becomes taller, leading to a greater force per unit area, hence greater pressure.
questions.hint: Think about how the weight of the water above changes with depth.
questions.subject: upbo8-physics

questions.question: A force of 300 N is applied perpendicularly on a surface having an area of 0.25 m². Calculate the pressure exerted on the surface.

options.text: 75 Pa
options.explanation: Incorrect. This would be the result if the area were 4 m² (300/4 = 75).

options.text: 120 Pa
options.explanation: Incorrect. This would be the result if the area were 2.5 m² (300/2.5 = 120).

options.text: 750 Pa
options.explanation: Incorrect. This would be the result if the area were 0.4 m² (300/0.4 = 750).

questions.explanation: The formula for pressure is P = Force / Area. Given Force (F) = 300 N and Area (A) = 0.25 m², P = 300 / 0.25 = 1200 Pa.
questions.hint: Use the formula P = F/A and substitute the given values.

questions.question: Assertion (A): It is impossible to suck a cold drink through a straw on the surface of the Moon. Reason (R): There is no atmosphere on the Moon to exert pressure.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Correct. The assertion and reason are both true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The reason does correctly explain the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The assertion is true, and the reason is also true.

questions.explanation: Sucking liquid through a straw works by reducing the air pressure inside the straw. The higher atmospheric pressure outside then pushes the liquid up into the straw and into your mouth. On the Moon, there is no atmosphere, meaning no external atmospheric pressure to push the liquid up. Therefore, the assertion is true, and the reason correctly explains why it is impossible.
questions.hint: Consider how a straw works and the role of atmospheric pressure.
